CLOSED GUARD GI FUNDAMENTALS GO FURTHE.overview: John Danaher's gi closed guard fundamentals, eight volumes and about 9.5 hours. He frames closed guard around six vulnerabilities in the top player's posture and organises the attacks by what the opponent does with their arms and knees. Volumes 1 and 2 are theory: what the closed guard is for, who is really in control, and holding the position. Volume 3 is a long section on the side scissor (getting the elbow across the centreline). Volume 4 covers the top lock and the armbar from guard. Volumes 5 and 6 are sweeps: the flower sweep and hip sweep when the knees are on the floor, and the scissor sweep variations. Volume 7 covers the clamp, the trap triangle and the overhead sweep. Volume 8 covers attacking a standing opponent, including omoplata sweeps.
CLOSED GUARD GI FUNDAMENTALS GO FURTHE.for: Gi players at any level who want a principled closed guard.

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' pin escapes in four volumes (about 2h 45m). Volume 1 sets out his escape mindset: chaining small movements into big ones and never accepting the position. Volume 2 covers side control (hip escape, reverse hip escape, running man with wrist control). Volume 3 covers mount (knee-elbow escape, bridge and roll, and the kipping escape, with detailed timing). Volume 4 covers back escapes, including dealing with double unders and the body triangle.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi players who get stuck under side control, mount or the back.
key: Mount escapes including the kipping escape
Back escapes against double unders and body triangle

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' submission escapes in four volumes (about 3 hours). Volume 1 covers the mindset: staying calm, understanding the attacker's next step and the stages of a submission. Volume 2 is armbar defence at each stage (jumping over the leg, stacking, the choi bar escape). Volume 3 covers the omoplata, straight ankle lock and rear naked choke, plus a bonus on being an annoying training partner. Volume 4 covers rotational escapes and closed guard submissions, especially triangle escapes and posture.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Anyone who gets tapped by the same submissions repeatedly; written for no-gi.
key: Omoplata, straight ankle lock and RNC defence

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones' heel hook defence course in six volumes (about 5h 15m), one of the most popular leg lock defence series. It starts with principles, calming down and testing the tap safely, then heel slipping (using your second leg, the 'two foot problem'), then late-stage cross ashi defences (the tombstone, 'defeating double trouble'). Later volumes cover the saddle, outside heel hooks (including standing and split-squat escapes from ashi) and advanced concepts: submission chains, kneeling versus standing defence and defending from open guard.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: No-gi players who freeze when someone grabs their leg.
key: Testing the tap and staying calm

Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.overview: Craig Jones on escaping front headlock chokes, including details he has taught to UFC champion Alexander Volkanovski. Volume 1 covers key concepts, the arm-in guillotine and the chin strap. Volume 2 covers escapes when mounted or in half guard, and defending the guillotine when you shoot a double leg. Volume 3 covers the high elbow guillotine (Marcelotine) and side control dangers. Volume 4 covers the anaconda and darce, including deep versions.
Craig Jones - COMPLETE Collection - as o.for: Wrestlers and no-gi players who shoot and get caught in front chokes; MMA athletes.
key: Arm-in guillotine and chin strap escapes
